text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian Federation Prime Minister Izudin Kapetanovic calls on High Representative Carl Bildt and NATO commander in Bosnia U.S. Admiral Joseph Lopez to undertake urgent measures to assure freedom of movement in area of Brcko.

- Michael Steiner, deputy to High Representative's office in Bosnia, expresses concern about blockage in process of return of refugees to Bosnia at Joint Civilian Commission meeting held in Modrica on Thursday.
- A $40 million project of independent broadcasting network TV-IN sponsored by U.S. businessman George Soros and EU will start broadcasting its programme in Bosnia on September 7.
- UNHCR starts project to repair 2,000 flats in Sarajevo, Kris Janowski, UNHCR spokesman, says in Sarajevo on Thursday.
- Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic, in meeting with Kenneth Scott, OSCE deputy to chief of mission, asks for general elections in Bosnia to be held on 14-15 September.
- International telephone system (EWST) starts operating in Sarajevo from Thursday.
